02

The Challenge

Problem

Culture is invisible, so it is hard to sell

Visitors had to understand what a culture audit is, tell four similar survey products apart, and trust a research framework, all before they would contact the team.

Client brief

“Keep it white, calm and not too colourful.”

The client wanted a clean white website that felt warm and human. Bright, loud colours were ruled out from day one, so warmth had to come from soft tones, imagery and type.

A

Explain the offer

Make four products easy to compare.

B

Build trust

Show the method, clients and scale early.

C

Capture leads

Low-effort contact and newsletter sign-up.

D

Serve clients

One-click login for survey admins.

03

Research & Insights

5stakeholder interviews with the client team
8culture & engagement platforms reviewed
3user personas defined
20+reference sites in the moodboard
Insight 01

Buyers need proof before they reach out

HR leaders look for a trusted method, client names and scale first. This shaped the proof stack on the home page.

Insight 02

The products were easy to confuse

Four survey products sounded alike. Grouping them in a mega menu with short descriptions made the differences clear.

Insight 03

Competitors felt loud

Most platforms use bright, saturated colours and busy dashboards. A calm white site helps this brand feel thoughtful and premium.

Insight 04

The science builds confidence

Showing the Denison model visually answered the question “why should we trust this?” better than long text.

User personas

HR & People leaderWhich survey do I actually need?

Compares options. Needs clear product differences, the process, and a sound method.

CXO / decision makerIs this worth the investment?

Skims fast. Looks for scale, known clients and a credible framework.

Client survey adminLet me get to my dashboard.

Returns often. Wants login one click away, with no distractions.

05

Design Principles

Four rules, agreed with the client after research, guided every screen.

Calm

White space first

Plenty of white, one idea per section, nothing competing for attention.

Warm

Human, not corporate

Real team photos, soft blush washes and one handwritten word per headline.

Proof

Show, then ask

The method, clients and numbers come before any call to action.

Clear

One next step

Each page ends in one obvious action: assess, contact or subscribe.

08

Colour System

White leads, navy anchors, and warm tints add softness. Coral is the only bright colour, and it is used for a single word at a time.

Hover or tap a colour to explore it. Click the hex code to copy it.

01 White
Base

Page background, cards and forms. Gives photos and content room to breathe.

02 Navy
Primary

Buttons, key headings, links, footer. The colour of trust.

03 Blush
Warm wash

Soft left side of hero and section backgrounds. Adds warmth without colour.

04 Lilac
Cool wash

Right side of gradients, eyebrow pills and tags. Balances the warm blush.

05 Coral
Accent

One handwritten word per headline, e.g. “Tomorrow”. Never for body text.

06 Ink
Text

Headlines and body copy. A navy-tinted black, softer than pure black.

60% White · base20% Blush & Lilac · soft washes15% Navy · buttons, text, footer5% Coral · accent words

Why white first

The client asked for a clean, uncluttered look. A white base gives photos and content room to breathe.

Why navy

Deep blue reads as trustworthy and expert, which matters for a consultancy that handles sensitive people data.

Why warm tints and coral

Soft blush washes and a coral script accent add human warmth without making the site colourful.
